title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Top of page (end of §1, 'Général non-sens sur Frobenius'). We have a commutative square of topoi g∘f_X = f_Y∘g, with g: X→Y and 'Frobenius' endomorphisms f_X, f_Y. For a sheaf G on Y there is the canonical isomorphism c^G: f_X^* g^* G ≅ g^* f_Y^* G (1.4). Given a Frobenius structure F_G: f_Y^*G → G (1.5), apply g^* to get g^*(F_G): g^*f_Y^*G → g^*G. Composing gives (1.6) g^*(F_G)∘c^G: f_X^*(g^*G) → g^*G. So pulling back a sheaf with Frobenius structure gives a sheaf with Frobenius structure. This complements (1.1)-(1.3) on the previous page, which treat push-forward via the base-change map f_Y^*g_* → g_*f_X^*.

§2 is the abstraction. Let α, β: X' ⇉ X be two morphisms of topoi. Define L(α,β) as the category of pairs (E, F_E), with E a sheaf on X and F_E: α^*E → β^*E. A variant requires F_E to be an isomorphism.

In categorical terms, L(α,β) is the inserter of the two functors α^*, β^*: X → X' (for the iso version, the iso-inserter). The forgetful functor ω^*(E,F_E) = E preserves colimits and finite limits, because α^* and β^* do. The Proposition says L(α,β) is a topos and ω^* is the inverse-image functor of a geometric morphism ω: X → L(α,β).

The tautological maps F_E assemble into a natural transformation (ωα)^* = α^*ω^* → β^*ω^* = (ωβ)^*. In SGA4's convention (a 2-cell u→v is u_*→v_*, i.e. v^*→u^*), this is a 2-cell F: ωβ → ωα in Homtop(X', L(α,β)); in the iso version it is an isomorphism.

Universal property. For any topos Y, let Homtop(X,α,β;Y) be the category of pairs (φ: X→Y, f: φβ → φα). Grothendieck notes this is described via the two composition functors Homtop(X,Y) ⇉ Homtop(X',Y); it is their inserter. Then g ↦ (g∘ω, g*F) is a functor Homtop(L(α,β), Y) → Homtop(X,α,β;Y). The next page asserts it is an equivalence.

Thus L(α,β) is the lax coequalizer (coinserter) of α, β in the 2-category of topoi. The iso version is the pseudo-coequalizer. Both are computed as the corresponding lax or pseudo limit of the categories of sheaves.

The intended application is X' = X, β = id, α = Frobenius. L(α,id) is then the topos of objects with a Frobenius map α^*E → E, or with a Frobenius isomorphism. Thus 'sheaves with Frobenius structure', e.g. F-crystals when X is a crystalline topos, become the sheaves of a single topos. §1 then becomes functoriality of this topos.

The next page proves the topos property by checking Giraud's axioms. The only issue is a small generating family, handled via cartesian sections of a fibred topos (SGA4 VI, numbering cited as 'I 9.25', '9.21'), with the marginal note 'à vérifier'.
errors: Last displayed functor is written Homtop(L(α,β), X) → Homtop(X,α,β;Y); the source should be Homtop(L(α,β), Y). This is a slip by Grothendieck.

The Proposition is stated without proof here. The proof sketch on the next page (small generating family via fibred topoi, SGA4) is flagged 'à vérifier'. The statement is nevertheless correct: inserters of finite-limit-preserving, colimit-preserving functors between Grothendieck topoi are Grothendieck topoi.
Notation is inconsistent: L(α,β) here becomes G(α,β) on the next page; f_X'^* vs f_X^* in (1.4)/(1.6).

ideas.what: Pullback of a Frobenius structure along a morphism commuting with Frobenius: g^*(F_G)∘c^G: f_X^* g^* G → g^* G
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of F-modules / F-crystals under pullback
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Berthelot, Katz, Deligne in F-crystal and Weil-sheaf contexts)

ideas.what: Category of pairs (E, α^*E → β^*E) for two geometric morphisms α,β: X'⇉X is a topos, with ω: X → L(α,β)
ideas.modern_name: inserter of inverse-image functors = coinserter (lax coequalizer) in the 2-category of topoi; iso version = pseudo-coequalizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore on 2-colimits of topoi (SGA4 VI fibred topoi; Moerdijk; Johnstone's Elephant B3.4; Lurie HTT 6.3); Weil-sheaf special case Deligne (Weil II)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 VI treats limits of fibred topoi / cartesian sections; explicit lax coequalizer statement unsure

ideas.what: Universal property: Homtop(L(α,β),Y) ≃ {(φ: X→Y, f: φβ→φα)}, described as an inserter of Homtop(X,Y) ⇉ Homtop(X',Y)
Special case X'=X, β=id, α=Frobenius: topos of sheaves with Frobenius map/iso
ideas.modern_name: topos of Weil sheaves / F-sheaves; mapping-torus-type topos; Weil-étale topos over finite fields

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages 'objects with Frobenius structure' (iso or mere map, i.e. F-crystal-like or Cartier-like data) as the sheaves of a topos. This topos is defined as the lax/pseudo coequalizer of Frobenius and the identity, with a 2-categorical universal property. This anticipates the descriptions of Weil-sheaf / Weil-étale topoi as homotopy quotients by Frobenius, and gives a topos for non-invertible F-structures.
missed.quote: Considérons la catégorie L(α,β) dont les objets sont les couples (E, F_E), où E ∈ Ob X, F_E : α^*(E) → β^*(E) [resp. F_E un isom] ... Prop L(α,β) est un topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Lax (non-invertible) Frobenius quotients of topoi are rarely used. A topos whose abelian sheaves are F-modules or Cartier modules would give cohomology of F-crystals and unit F-modules as topos cohomology, with functoriality for free. The pseudo version matches Weil-étale constructions, but the early date (1965-69) for the general coinserter formulation is not recorded.

missed.claim: The topos property is proven only in sketch (marked 'à vérifier'), and the functorial dependence on (α,β) is begun on the next page but not visibly completed here.
missed.quote: et le foncteur évident g ↦ (g∘ω, g*F) Homtop(L(α,β), X) → Homtop(X,α,β;Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The result is now standard 2-categorical topos theory, but the intended crystalline application (topos of F-crystals) is not developed in the literature in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early formulation of the lax/pseudo coequalizer of two geometric morphisms with its universal property, motivated by Frobenius structures. Mathematically it is now folklore (coinserters in Topos, Weil-sheaf topoi), so only the dating and the crystalline motivation are of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: target is g^*(G), not f^*(G): 'g^*(F_G) : g^* f_Y^*(G) → g^*(G)'.
The bracket reads 'qui se décrit astucieusement à l'aide des Homtop(X,Y) ⇉ Homtop(X',Y)' (plausible reading).
